chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said:
I had dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'The dinner after the last Isha prayer is the dinner of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the last Isha prayer (referring to the night prayer)
key_terms.تَعَشَّيْتُ: I had dinner (specifically the late evening meal)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of having dinner after the Isha prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the late evening meal (Ta'shir) to a prophetic tradition, linking it specifically to the time after the final Isha prayer. This highlights the spiritual and physical benefits of maintaining a routine aligned with the Sunnah of the Prophets, emphasizing moderation and the sanctity of daily sustenance within Shia jurisprudence.
